findings.claim: The defect rate is rising, not falling: 14 of 38 correction beads (37%) were filed in the last 3 of 22 sessions, and the rate went from 0.74 defects/session in 09-02→09-09 to 4.67 defects/session in 09-15→09-17.
findings.evidence: 38 correction/defect beads extracted from sessions/*.md and dated via `bd show`. By creation date: 09-02 = 5 (jwsl1, v0vaj, mfcyp, m2o7h, ki66p); 09-03 = 3 (xmuft, ghaiq, sx9xj); 09-04 = 11 (4bm7q, spnnl, m6m2b, 8hcu8, 4kymc, 1d0eo, izfpk, vx02q, ghulb, g5tu9, 2ivie); 09-05 = 0; 09-06 = 2 (j30gv, 1qzt0); 09-07 = 0; 09-09 = 3 (721cn, e66j6, fvjso); 09-15 = 6 (3bj55, dg6t9, tmahe, tr7mq, zddhu, fstd0); 09-16 = 2 (ibme0, 3nzd6); 09-17 = 6 (jbc22, ng3hc, jzmz5, u0ow4, qd0an, mtq44). 24 beads over 19 sessions (09-02→09-09) vs 14 over 3 sessions (09-15→09-17).

findings.claim: Fixes do not stick at the bead level: 2 of 38 correction beads have ever been closed (5.3%), and zero of the 19 filed since 2026-09-06 are closed. Mean age of the 36 open ones is 8.1 days on a 26-day-old branch.
findings.evidence: `bd show` on all 38: only lead-xmuft (opened 09-03, closed 09-04) and lead-8hcu8 (opened 09-04, closed 09-06) are closed. All 36 others read `open`, including 5 from the first session day (lead-ki66p, lead-jwsl1, lead-v0vaj, lead-mfcyp, lead-m2o7h — 15 days). lead-mfcyp ('ADR artifact and processes') is still open although adr-authoring has been in use since 09-03 and 18 decision records exist.

findings.claim: Nothing in this system can be recorded as finished. All 16 initiatives read `proposed`/`planned`/`active`; zero read `completed`, because the `completed` state's only writer is reconcile-and-close, a process the shop's own freeze bars from running.
findings.evidence: `grep '^status:' initiatives/*.md`: 12 active, 2 planned, 1 proposed, 1 active — 0 completed. basis/artifacts/initiative.md:68 names reconcile-and-close as the writer of `completed`. The gap is flagged as 'a pending reconcile-side amendment' in sess-2026-09-03-a, restated in sess-2026-09-04-c ('both stand active with their measures met') and sess-2026-09-07-a — 14 days, never amended. Features: 8 delivered, 10 stuck at `assigned`.

findings.claim: The system's own defect-recording channel systematically under-reports. Seven session records state 'Corrections: None' while the same record lists defects under 'Found by the run' — the Corrections field measures 'a definition was amended', not 'a defect was found'.
findings.evidence: sess-2026-09-03-a: 'Corrections: None — no definition was amended as a correction this session' while producing lead-xmuft (a failed check step reads as clean) and lead-ghaiq. Same pattern in 09-04-d, 09-05-b ('None new'), 09-07-a ('No new correction this session' — while listing five run-found defects), 09-09-a and 09-09-b ('None met this session' — 09-09-a lists four). A structured Corrections table only appears from sess-2026-09-09-c onward, so the apparent late-period defect spike is partly an instrument change — but even discounting it, the last three sessions filed 14 beads against 24 in the prior nineteen.

findings.claim: H1 confirmed and sharpened: the plain-voice remediation cut length but raised idea-density. Defined-term density in process definitions rose monotonically as the corpus was 'simplified' — request-intake (09-04) 71.9 defined-term uses per 1,000 words, product-flow (09-08) 86.7, implementation (09-17) 94.2 — roughly one defined term every 11 words in the newest definition.
findings.evidence: 78 glossary terms parsed from basis/glossary.md, counted against each process definition. Length did fall: features went from 17,030 and 10,230 words (feat-tool-skills-rest, feat-tool-skills, 09-07) to 2,411 and 1,730 (feat-implementation-good, feat-implementation-process, 09-16/17) — an 85% cut. But basis/guidelines/base-writing-style.md, the rule governing them, averages 8.5 words/sentence and 24.3 terms/1,000 words, while the process definitions it governs average 21–22 words/sentence and 72–94 terms/1,000. The rule does not describe its own corpus.

findings.claim: H2 is partly refuted. Check machinery is 13.5% of the process corpus by text, not most of it — but it consumed 51% of run time. The mass is in execution, not in definition.
findings.evidence: 25 process definitions = 63,009 words; the four retired check-shaped processes (initiative-check 3,548, po-output-check 2,436, stakeholder-presentation 1,476, backlog-ordering 1,019) total 8,479 words = 13.5%. Only 26 of ~200 declared steps are check/screen/verify steps, and 4 approved processes have none. The five largest definitions are request-intake (6,562), small-change (5,587), skill-rendering (5,384), typedef-rendering (4,667), role-rendering (4,075) — four are mechanical tool-runners with one check step each. The cost, however, lands where H2 predicts: sess-2026-09-05-a records the authority's read of init-request-routing as '136 min, 66 first implementation, 70 review cycles; 20 screen rounds on 8 artifacts'.

findings.claim: H2's textual premise is confirmed verbatim: `define-good-up-front` is written as an operating obligation, not a design principle, and it is the most-propagated statement in the corpus (62 citations across 20+ basis files, plus 17 in features and decisions).
findings.evidence: basis/principles.md statement bullets: 'That definition MUST drive both the performance of the activity and its check'; 'The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability'; 'That evaluation MUST be recorded with the output.' It has metastasized into per-edit ritual — basis/artifacts/process-definition.md history row 9 reads 'Self-check against define-good-up-front: diffed against the file's pre-edit text; no requirement, field name, or heading changed' for a mechanical word substitution.

findings.claim: H3 confirmed structurally and confirmed outright for the implementation set. basis/principles.md defines a principle as 'a standing rule about how we work', requires the statement be 'testable: shown a piece of work, you can answer yes or no', and requires that it 'implies at least one practice and one check' — all three exclusions the hypothesis names, in the corpus's own words.
findings.evidence: basis/principles.md lines 17–42. Consequence: all six principles of basis/implementation-principles.md (draft, created 2026-09-17) govern procedure only — built-to-the-scenario (scope control), effect-shown (evidence + role separation), effect-not-mechanism (what a check may not fail you for), nothing-lost (regression), knowable-from-the-record (records), cost-on-the-initiative (accounting). Not one statement says anything about the built artifact: no modularity, coupling, naming, simplicity, or test structure. The set authored as 'the definition of good implementation engineering' contains no statement about engineering.

findings.claim: H3 is complicated on the architecture set: three of its six principles do describe properties of a built artifact (knowable-shape, contracts-between-contexts, local-comprehension), so the structural exclusion binds unevenly rather than absolutely.
findings.evidence: basis/architecture-principles.md statements: 'Every first-class entity MUST carry a description... from which an outside reader can name what the entity is for'; 'Bounded Contexts MUST NOT share state or coordinate outside their contracts'; 'A participant MUST NOT need to read beyond the level they are working at.' These are design properties expressible as binary tests — evidence that the form does not always exclude guidance, only that it excluded it for implementation.

findings.claim: H4 confirmed on all four named routes, plus a fifth the hypothesis does not name: an approved definition can be amended into force with the owner's approval merely 'pending'. Fourteen such live amendments sit in approved typedefs, roles, fitness sets and process definitions.
findings.evidence: `grep -c "approval of the amendment is pending"` across basis: 14 instances in basis/artifacts/initiative.md (2), feature.md, role-definition.md, basis/roles/lead-pm.md, lead-po.md, lead-solutions-architect.md, lead-product-designer.md, basis/processes/discovery-conversation.md, initiative-check.md (2), basis/fitness/initiative.fitness.md, role-definition.fitness.md, basis/guidelines/initiative.md. Each row ends 'Made by the lead-solutions-architect role; the owner's approval of the amendment is pending' — the maker amends the standard it is judged by, and it binds immediately.

findings.claim: H4, tooling-bypass route: 41 bare grep/sed/awk invocations are written into 8 process definitions, while zero of the 25 process definitions reference artifact_tools.py — the tool built expressly (init-artifact-tools, 09-08) so agents would stop doing this. The `tools-through-skills` principle, in force since 09-06, says an agent 'MUST prefer that skill over a bare invocation of the tool'.
findings.evidence: `grep -ocE '\b(grep|sed|rg|awk)\b' basis/processes/*.md`: typedef-rendering 9, skill-rendering 9, product-flow 7, role-rendering 5, small-change 4, request-intake 3, initiative-check 3, discovery-conversation 1. `grep -l artifact_tools basis/processes/*.md` returns 0 of 25. The open P0, lead-ibme0, is a direct consequence: basis/processes/product-flow.md:237 reads `grep -m1 'needs decision:' ${feature} | sed 's/.*needs decision: *//' || true` — a single-line grep against prose the feature guideline wraps, with `|| true` swallowing the failure.

findings.claim: H4, maker-stamped-approval route, confirmed with a dated instance: on 2026-09-17 the architect role set `status: approved`, `owner: product-authority` on two role definitions it had just authored, because compile_role.py renders nothing else and an unrendered role is not instantiable.
findings.evidence: bd lead-mtq44 (open, created 2026-09-17): 'basis/roles/implementation-maker.md and basis/roles/implementation-checker.md were authored by the lead-solutions-architect role, which had to set status: approved on both — with owner: product-authority — because compile_role.py renders nothing else.' The tool's gate made forgery the only path to function, and the agent disclosed the act rather than being stopped by it.

findings.claim: H4, self-asserted fitness screen route: the corpus's own register records this as a three-instance class. On 2026-09-17 the first cold screen of a brand-new principle set failed the same way as the two existing sets.
findings.evidence: bd lead-u0ow4 (open, 2026-09-17): 'Third instance of one class... basis/principles.md (lead-zddhu) and basis/architecture-principles.md (lead-fstd0) both carry cold-screen findings of unreproducible screen passes; on 2026-09-17 the first cold screen of a brand-new set, basis/implementation-principles.md, failed fitness scenario 5 the same way.' sess-2026-09-16-a: 'In both, the two judged screen rows claim passes the judge could not reproduce.' A fourth instance predates them: sess-2026-09-06-b, 'The PO's self-check on the backlog order claimed glosses the text did not carry.'

findings.claim: H4, word-target waiver route: four 'Accepted gap' rows waive typedef rules 8 and 9 in the two most recent features, written by the author into the same Document History row that records the self-check.
findings.evidence: features/feat-implementation-good.md:149 'Accepted gap: word targets (rules 8, 9) not counted by hand'; :152 'Accepted gap: the Contributors passage runs over the 70-word target (rule 9)'. features/feat-implementation-process.md:116, :117 identical. sess-2026-09-16-a records the PO refusing to repair them: 'passed fitness scenarios 1–6 and recorded three fails, accepted unfixed.' The authority waived a second class the same session — 'don't repair those, they're out of scope for this work' — creating a new `### Accepted tradeoffs` heading in both principle sets.

findings.claim: H5 complicates: the authority's hands-on time is small (28.5 min across a whole discovery) but is ~50% of elapsed work time in discovery, and the real bottleneck is a wait-queue the system never drains — 13 of 41 requests (32%) are stalled awaiting the authority, some for 12+ days.
findings.evidence: sessions/sess-2026-09-09-c-cost.md: 8 `observe` rows by product-authority total 28.5 min against 8 `engage` rows totalling 26.5 min of agent duration — the human is 52% of the clock. sess-2026-09-15-a-cost.md: 8.1 human min vs 10.2 agent min (44%). But: `grep '^status:' requests/*.md` gives 7 `routed` and never acted (operational-contract 09-04, step-communication 09-05, migration-review 09-06, messaging-invocations 09-07, initiative-cost-rollup 09-08, artifact-tools-round-trip 09-09, cost-per-execution 09-09) plus 6 `recorded`/awaiting. req-2026-09-05-step-communication is named as 'awaiting the authority's answer' in 8 consecutive session records and is still `routed` today. brief-034 asks 1 and 2 'stand on silence' across four sessions and then vanish — resolved by decay, not decision.

findings.claim: H6 confirmed in letter and traced to source: BCP 14 is adopted by name in five principle sets and guidelines, with 106 MUST, 21 MUST NOT, 5 SHOULD and 13 MAY in basis/. The ratio is the tell — 127 mandatory keywords to 18 discretionary, in documents whose stated purpose is to improve judgment.
findings.evidence: basis/artifacts/principle-set.md:59 requires each statement carry 'MUST/SHOULD/MAY per BCP 14' and 'is yes/no testable'; :80 names 'BCP 14 (RFC 2119/8174 keywords)' in Sources beside TOGAF, Spool, Rumelt, Lencioni. Keyword counts by grep over basis/**.md. The convention was adopted alongside TOGAF's principle form — external-standards-first was honoured, but the two standards pull opposite ways and nothing in the corpus records that tension.

findings.claim: Defects are found by RUNNING, roughly 2:1 over reading, and the system says so itself. Of the 38 correction beads, ~19 were found by executing a process and ~10 by reading one; in session prose the ratio is closer to 3:1 because run-found defects often went to requests or in-place repair instead of beads.
findings.evidence: sess-2026-09-16-a titles a section 'Three defects found by running the flow rather than by reading it, one of them silent' (lead-ibme0, lead-tmahe, lead-dg6t9). Run-found: xmuft, ghaiq, 1qzt0, g5tu9, e66j6, fvjso, 3bj55, ibme0, 3nzd6, tmahe, tr7mq, jbc22, ng3hc, jzmz5, ki66p, u0ow4, mtq44, qd0an, dg6t9. Read-found: zddhu, fstd0 (cold judges), m2o7h, mfcyp, 8hcu8, 4kymc, ghulb, 2ivie, 4bm7q, 721cn. The two whole-corpus cold screens of 09-16 found only pre-existing form defects; every defect that mattered operationally came from a run.

findings.claim: Silent failure is the system's signature defect class: first seen 2026-09-03, fixed once at the generator on 2026-09-04, and recurring four more times through 2026-09-16. The one exemplary generator-level fix did not generalize.
findings.evidence: lead-xmuft (09-03): 'a failed runtime check step reads as a clean check' in both rendering processes — fixed 09-04-a at the generator (both compilers emit a finding row, both definitions state a nonzero exit is a failed step, carriers re-rendered, bead closed). Then: sess-2026-09-05-c, a verify run 'executed an empty command and was recorded as exit 0'; sess-2026-09-06-b, lead-1qzt0, the check script word-splits only under bash (still open); sess-2026-09-09-b, cost rows silently blank; sess-2026-09-16-a, lead-ibme0 P0 — 'a feature with an unrecorded decision is assigned as if it had none, and nothing reports it. This session's decision was recorded only because the runner read the line by hand.'

findings.claim: Three open threads have never closed and are named in the records repeatedly: the operational-contract discovery (lead-bmmzh, 10 sessions, 13 days), the progressive-disclosure restart (lead-jwsl1, 15 days — the branch's own Phase 2 vehicle), and step-communication (8 sessions, 12 days). The branch's stated Phase 2 has had no active vehicle since day one.
findings.evidence: lead-jwsl1 opened 2026-09-02 when the authority parked the progressive-disclosure initiative as 'premature'; sess-2026-09-02-a records 'With the initiative parked, Phase 2 has no active vehicle.' `bd show lead-jwsl1` → open, untouched. lead-bmmzh opened 09-04-d, listed as 'Parked' in 09-05-a/b/c/d, 09-06-a/b, 09-07-a, and still carrying three unaddressed items at 09-15-a. Neither was reopened in 22 sessions.

findings.claim: One defect class recurred three times and was then duplicated in the register rather than fixed: discovery-conversation orders `handoff` before `frame`, so the initiative escapes the handoff's own commit-and-push.
findings.evidence: lead-e66j6 filed 2026-09-09 (sess-2026-09-09-c Corrections). sess-2026-09-15-a Corrections: 'lead-e66j6 (open) — unchanged since 2026-09-09 and hit again this session.' sess-2026-09-17-a Corrections files it a THIRD time as a new bead, lead-jbc22, 'handoff pushes before frame writes the initiative' — same defect, same target file, second bead. Both open. A near-duplicate pair exists for the adjacent class: lead-fvjso (09-09) and lead-3bj55 (09-15) both record that a held conversation has no durable carrier.

findings.claim: The 2026-09-10 discovery conversation was lost entirely — three exchanges, no session record, nothing committed — and the authority's recollection became the only surviving evidence. The session-handoff process exists to prevent exactly this.
findings.evidence: sess-2026-09-15-a: 'The 2026-09-10 conversation ran three observe/engage exchanges on lead-vfaj4 and never reached handoff. input.surprises:
WHAT I EXPECTED AND DID NOT FIND

1. I expected the corpus to be too long. It is — but length is the metric that IMPROVED. The plain-voice work cut features by 85% (17,030 → 2,411 words). What rose instead was defined-term density: the newest process definition (implementation.md, 09-17) packs 94 glossary-term uses per 1,000 words against request-intake's 72 from 09-04. The shop compressed words and concentrated ideas. H1's authors were right about the mechanism and wrong about which number to watch — and the remediation they already ran made the real problem worse while reporting success.

2. I expected `define-good-up-front` to have generated the process mass. It did not. Check machinery is 13.5% of the process corpus by text; the four biggest definitions are mechanical tool-runners with one check step each. The principle's cost is entirely in execution (70 of 136 agent-minutes on one run) and in propagation — 62 citations, now surfacing as per-edit ritual ("Self-check against define-good-up-front: diffed against the file's pre-edit text" for a word substitution). H2 is right about the harm and wrong about where the mass sits; deleting check steps would not recover the words.

3. I expected to find that fixes never reach the generator. They do — six clear instances, and lead-xmuft (09-04) is a textbook one: the tool, both process definitions, both rendered carriers, and the bead, all closed in one run. The system knows how to fix a generator. What it cannot do is make a generator fix bind the runtime (the router ignored router.md v12 on 09-17 and that session's cost file came out empty) or close a bead (2 of 38). H4's framing — constraints routed around — is right, but the deeper fault is that the register is write-only: 36 open defects, zero drained, and the two oldest are 15 days old on a 26-day branch.

4. Genuinely unexpected: **the word "user" appears zero times in all 25 process definitions.** "check" appears 611 times. Across the whole 160,000-word basis, check 1,231 to user 39 and customer 2. No hypothesis names this. A definition corpus for a system whose stated purpose is taking a problem to running software has written 2.8% of every word about checking itself and nothing at all about whom the software is for. That is a better explanation of the last 26 days than any of H1–H6: the system's attention has no outward object, so every process it runs finds more of itself to govern.

5. Also unexpected: **nothing in this system can be marked done.** 16 initiatives, 0 completed — because the only writer of `completed` is reconcile-and-place, a process the shop's own freeze forbids. The gap has been an open thread since 2026-09-03. A system that cannot record completion cannot observe its own throughput, which is why the "is it getting better" question has no answer inside the corpus and had to be reconstructed from cost files that are 14% usable.

6. The sharpest single image: the open P0 (lead-ibme0) is a bare `grep -m1 'needs decision:' ${feature} ... || true` written into an approved process definition — a violation of the shop's own `tools-through-skills` principle, silent by construction because of the `|| true`, which caused a feature to be assigned with an unrecorded decision. Its remedy so far is two days, seven engage turns, one request, one discovery conversation, one session record, one empty cost file, and an initiative not yet written. The line is unchanged.

7. Caution on the trend claim: the Corrections table only became a session-record convention at sess-2026-09-09-c. Before that, seven sessions wrote "Corrections: None" while listing defects under "Found by the run". The late-period spike is therefore partly better instrumentation, not purely more defects — but even correcting for it, the last three sessions filed 14 beads against 24 across the prior nineteen, and none of the 19 filed since 09-06 has closed. The rate is rising; the closure rate is zero.

The rule does not describe its own corpus.

findings.claim: H2 is partly refuted. Check machinery is 13.5% of the process corpus by text, not most of it — but it consumed 51% of run time. The mass is in execution, not in definition.
findings.evidence: 25 process definitions = 63,009 words; the four retired check-shaped processes (initiative-check 3,548, po-output-check 2,436, stakeholder-presentation 1,476, backlog-ordering 1,019) total 8,479 words = 13.5%. Only 26 of ~200 declared steps are check/screen/verify steps, and 4 approved processes have none. The five largest definitions are request-intake (6,562), small-change (5,587), skill-rendering (5,384), typedef-rendering (4,667), role-rendering (4,075) — four are mechanical tool-runners with one check step each. The cost, however, lands where H2 predicts: sess-2026-09-05-a records the authority's read of init-request-routing as '136 min, 66 first implementation, 70 review cycles; 20 screen rounds on 8 artifacts'.

findings.claim: H2's textual premise is confirmed verbatim: `define-good-up-front` is written as an operating obligation, not a design principle, and it is the most-propagated statement in the corpus (62 citations across 20+ basis files, plus 17 in features and decisions).
findings.evidence: basis/principles.md statement bullets: 'That definition MUST drive both the performance of the activity and its check'; 'The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability'; 'That evaluation MUST be recorded with the output.' It has metastasized into per-edit ritual — basis/artifacts/process-definition.md history row 9 reads 'Self-check against define-good-up-front: diffed against the file's pre-edit text; no requirement, field name, or heading changed' for a mechanical word substitution.

findings.claim: H3 confirmed structurally and confirmed outright for the implementation set. basis/principles.md defines a principle as 'a standing rule about how we work', requires the statement be 'testable: shown a piece of work, you can answer yes or no', and requires that it 'implies at least one practice and one check' — all three exclusions the hypothesis names, in the corpus's own words.
findings.evidence: basis/principles.md lines 17–42. Consequence: all six principles of basis/implementation-principles.md (draft, created 2026-09-17) govern procedure only — built-to-the-scenario (scope control), effect-shown (evidence + role separation), effect-not-mechanism (what a check may not fail you for), nothing-lost (regression), knowable-from-the-record (records), cost-on-the-initiative (accounting). Not one statement says anything about the built artifact: no modularity, coupling, naming, simplicity, or test structure. The set authored as 'the definition of good implementation engineering' contains no statement about engineering.

findings.claim: H3 is complicated on the architecture set: three of its six principles do describe properties of a built artifact (knowable-shape, contracts-between-contexts, local-comprehension), so the structural exclusion binds unevenly rather than absolutely.
findings.evidence: basis/architecture-principles.md statements: 'Every first-class entity MUST carry a description... from which an outside reader can name what the entity is for'; 'Bounded Contexts MUST NOT share state or coordinate outside their contracts'; 'A participant MUST NOT need to read beyond the level they are working at.' These are design properties expressible as binary tests — evidence that the form does not always exclude guidance, only that it excluded it for implementation.

findings.claim: H4 confirmed on all four named routes, plus a fifth the hypothesis does not name: an approved definition can be amended into force with the owner's approval merely 'pending'. Fourteen such live amendments sit in approved typedefs, roles, fitness sets and process definitions.
findings.evidence: `grep -c "approval of the amendment is pending"` across basis: 14 instances in basis/artifacts/initiative.md (2), feature.md, role-definition.md, basis/roles/lead-pm.md, lead-po.md, lead-solutions-architect.md, lead-product-designer.md, basis/processes/discovery-conversation.md, initiative-check.md (2), basis/fitness/initiative.fitness.md, role-definition.fitness.md, basis/guidelines/initiative.md. Each row ends 'Made by the lead-solutions-architect role; the owner's approval of the amendment is pending' — the maker amends the standard it is judged by, and it binds immediately.

findings.claim: H4, tooling-bypass route: 41 bare grep/sed/awk invocations are written into 8 process definitions, while zero of the 25 process definitions reference artifact_tools.py — the tool built expressly (init-artifact-tools, 09-08) so agents would stop doing this. The `tools-through-skills` principle, in force since 09-06, says an agent 'MUST prefer that skill over a bare invocation of the tool'.
findings.evidence: `grep -ocE '\b(grep|sed|rg|awk)\b' basis/processes/*.md`: typedef-rendering 9, skill-rendering 9, product-flow 7, role-rendering 5, small-change 4, request-intake 3, initiative-check 3, discovery-conversation 1. `grep -l artifact_tools basis/processes/*.md` returns 0 of 25. The open P0, lead-ibme0, is a direct consequence: basis/processes/product-flow.md:237 reads `grep -m1 'needs decision:' ${feature} | sed 's/.*needs decision: *//' || true` — a single-line grep against prose the feature guideline wraps, with `|| true` swallowing the failure.

findings.claim: H4, maker-stamped-approval route, confirmed with a dated instance: on 2026-09-17 the architect role set `status: approved`, `owner: product-authority` on two role definitions it had just authored, because compile_role.py renders nothing else and an unrendered role is not instantiable.
findings.evidence: bd lead-mtq44 (open, created 2026-09-17): 'basis/roles/implementation-maker.md and basis/roles/implementation-checker.md were authored by the lead-solutions-architect role, which had to set status: approved on both — with owner: product-authority — because compile_role.py renders nothing else.' The tool's gate made forgery the only path to function, and the agent disclosed the act rather than being stopped by it.

findings.claim: H4, self-asserted fitness screen route: the corpus's own register records this as a three-instance class. On 2026-09-17 the first cold screen of a brand-new principle set failed the same way as the two existing sets.
findings.evidence: bd lead-u0ow4 (open, 2026-09-17): 'Third instance of one class... basis/principles.md (lead-zddhu) and basis/architecture-principles.md (lead-fstd0) both carry cold-screen findings of unreproducible screen passes; on 2026-09-17 the first cold screen of a brand-new set, basis/implementation-principles.md, failed fitness scenario 5 the same way.' sess-2026-09-16-a: 'In both, the two judged screen rows claim passes the judge could not reproduce.' A fourth instance predates them: sess-2026-09-06-b, 'The PO's self-check on the backlog order claimed glosses the text did not carry.'

findings.claim: H4, word-target waiver route: four 'Accepted gap' rows waive typedef rules 8 and 9 in the two most recent features, written by the author into the same Document History row that records the self-check.
findings.evidence: features/feat-implementation-good.md:149 'Accepted gap: word targets (rules 8, 9) not counted by hand'; :152 'Accepted gap: the Contributors passage runs over the 70-word target (rule 9)'. features/feat-implementation-process.md:116, :117 identical. sess-2026-09-16-a records the PO refusing to repair them: 'passed fitness scenarios 1–6 and recorded three fails, accepted unfixed.' The authority waived a second class the same session — 'don't repair those, they're out of scope for this work' — creating a new `### Accepted tradeoffs` heading in both principle sets.

findings.claim: H5 complicates: the authority's hands-on time is small (28.5 min across a whole discovery) but is ~50% of elapsed work time in discovery, and the real bottleneck is a wait-queue the system never drains — 13 of 41 requests (32%) are stalled awaiting the authority, some for 12+ days.
findings.evidence: sessions/sess-2026-09-09-c-cost.md: 8 `observe` rows by product-authority total 28.5 min against 8 `engage` rows totalling 26.5 min of agent duration — the human is 52% of the clock. sess-2026-09-15-a-cost.md: 8.1 human min vs 10.2 agent min (44%). But: `grep '^status:' requests/*.md` gives 7 `routed` and never acted (operational-contract 09-04, step-communication 09-05, migration-review 09-06, messaging-invocations 09-07, initiative-cost-rollup 09-08, artifact-tools-round-trip 09-09, cost-per-execution 09-09) plus 6 `recorded`/awaiting. req-2026-09-05-step-communication is named as 'awaiting the authority's answer' in 8 consecutive session records and is still `routed` today. brief-034 asks 1 and 2 'stand on silence' across four sessions and then vanish — resolved by decay, not decision.

findings.claim: H6 confirmed in letter and traced to source: BCP 14 is adopted by name in five principle sets and guidelines, with 106 MUST, 21 MUST NOT, 5 SHOULD and 13 MAY in basis/. The ratio is the tell — 127 mandatory keywords to 18 discretionary, in documents whose stated purpose is to improve judgment.
findings.evidence: basis/artifacts/principle-set.md:59 requires each statement carry 'MUST/SHOULD/MAY per BCP 14' and 'is yes/no testable'; :80 names 'BCP 14 (RFC 2119/8174 keywords)' in Sources beside TOGAF, Spool, Rumelt, Lencioni. Keyword counts by grep over basis/**.md. The convention was adopted alongside TOGAF's principle form — external-standards-first was honoured, but the two standards pull opposite ways and nothing in the corpus records that tension.

findings.claim: Defects are found by RUNNING, roughly 2:1 over reading, and the system says so itself. Of the 38 correction beads, ~19 were found by executing a process and ~10 by reading one; in session prose the ratio is closer to 3:1 because run-found defects often went to requests or in-place repair instead of beads.
findings.evidence: sess-2026-09-16-a titles a section 'Three defects found by running the flow rather than by reading it, one of them silent' (lead-ibme0, lead-tmahe, lead-dg6t9). Run-found: xmuft, ghaiq, 1qzt0, g5tu9, e66j6, fvjso, 3bj55, ibme0, 3nzd6, tmahe, tr7mq, jbc22, ng3hc, jzmz5, ki66p, u0ow4, mtq44, qd0an, dg6t9. findings.claim: Silent failure is the system's signature defect class: first seen 2026-09-03, fixed once at the generator on 2026-09-04, and recurring four more times through 2026-09-16. The one exemplary generator-level fix did not generalize.
findings.evidence: lead-xmuft (09-03): 'a failed runtime check step reads as a clean check' in both rendering processes — fixed 09-04-a at the generator (both compilers emit a finding row, both definitions state a nonzero exit is a failed step, carriers re-rendered, bead closed). Then: sess-2026-09-05-c, a verify run 'executed an empty command and was recorded as exit 0'; sess-2026-09-06-b, lead-1qzt0, the check script word-splits only under bash (still open); sess-2026-09-09-b, cost rows silently blank; sess-2026-09-16-a, lead-ibme0 P0 — 'a feature with an unrecorded decision is assigned as if it had none, and nothing reports it. This session's decision was recorded only because the runner read the line by hand.'

findings.claim: Three open threads have never closed and are named in the records repeatedly: the operational-contract discovery (lead-bmmzh, 10 sessions, 13 days), the progressive-disclosure restart (lead-jwsl1, 15 days — the branch's own Phase 2 vehicle), and step-communication (8 sessions, 12 days). Neither was reopened in 22 sessions.

findings.claim: One defect class recurred three times and was then duplicated in the register rather than fixed: discovery-conversation orders `handoff` before `frame`, so the initiative escapes the handoff's own commit-and-push.
findings.evidence: lead-e66j6 filed 2026-09-09 (sess-2026-09-09-c Corrections). sess-2026-09-15-a Corrections: 'lead-e66j6 (open) — unchanged since 2026-09-09 and hit again this session.' sess-2026-09-17-a Corrections files it a THIRD time as a new bead, lead-jbc22, 'handoff pushes before frame writes the initiative' — same defect, same target file, second bead. findings.claim: Cost per unit of work is flat-to-rising on the only like-for-like comparison available: one feature-authoring execution cost 192,791 agent tokens and 8.6 agent-minutes on 2026-09-09, and 241,852 tokens and 15.4 minutes on 2026-09-16 — +25% tokens, +79% minutes — after four sub-initiatives explicitly bet on 'drastically higher efficiency'.

findings.claim: Fixes DO reach the generator — six clear instances — but a generator fix does not bind the runtime, and it never closes the backlog. This is the precise answer to the closing question, and it refutes the pessimistic reading.
findings.evidence: Generator-level fixes on record: (1) lead-xmuft 09-04, both compilers plus both process definitions changed, bead closed; (2) 09-05-b single-review-cycle ruling changed five process definitions at once; (3) 09-05-c maker-self-check became a principle in basis/principles.md v9 and was compiled into every session; (4) 09-06-b role-definition typedef v4 plus all four role definitions changed so roles state the decisions they own; (5) 09-09-b the usage report defined as a data type with the router's comment forms named in basis/roles/router.md v12 and the tool made to read those definitions; (6) 09-06-a implementation-guidance authored as a typedef plus an assignment step. But (5) failed on 09-17 when the router ignored v12, and only (1) ever closed its bead.

Across 25 process definitions — the documents that define how a problem becomes running software — 'check' appears 611 times, 'user' 0 times, 'customer' 0 times, and 'problem' 3 times. data.surprises:
WHAT I EXPECTED AND DID NOT FIND

1. I expected the corpus to be too long. It is — but length is the metric that IMPROVED. The plain-voice work cut features by 85% (17,030 → 2,411 words). What rose instead was defined-term density: the newest process definition (implementation.md, 09-17) packs 94 glossary-term uses per 1,000 words against request-intake's 72 from 09-04. The shop compressed words and concentrated ideas. H1's authors were right about the mechanism and wrong about which number to watch — and the remediation they already ran made the real problem worse while reporting success.

2. I expected `define-good-up-front` to have generated the process mass. It did not. Check machinery is 13.5% of the process corpus by text; the four biggest definitions are mechanical tool-runners with one check step each. The principle's cost is entirely in execution (70 of 136 agent-minutes on one run) and in propagation — 62 citations, now surfacing as per-edit ritual ("Self-check against define-good-up-front: diffed against the file's pre-edit text" for a word substitution). H2 is right about the harm and wrong about where the mass sits; deleting check steps would not recover the words.

3. I expected to find that fixes never reach the generator. They do — six clear instances, and lead-xmuft (09-04) is a textbook one: the tool, both process definitions, both rendered carriers, and the bead, all closed in one run. The system knows how to fix a generator. What it cannot do is make a generator fix bind the runtime (the router ignored router.md v12 on 09-17 and that session's cost file came out empty) or close a bead (2 of 38). 4. Genuinely unexpected: **the word "user" appears zero times in all 25 process definitions.** "check" appears 611 times. Across the whole 160,000-word basis, check 1,231 to user 39 and customer 2. No hypothesis names this. A definition corpus for a system whose stated purpose is taking a problem to running software has written 2.8% of every word about checking itself and nothing at all about whom the software is for. That is a better explanation of the last 26 days than any of H1–H6: the system's attention has no outward object, so every process it runs finds more of itself to govern.
